intro.title: Build distributed lock for critical jobs
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a distributed lock system to prevent multiple instances of a Node.js application from running the same critical job simultaneously. You will learn the core concept of mutual exclusion in a distributed environment, ensuring only one process can execute a task at a time. The implementation will use Node.js's built-in modules and a simple file-based locking mechanism to simulate coordination across processes. By the end, you'll understand how to create, acquire, and release locks to manage critical jobs safely.
intro.usecase: Distributed locks are essential in production systems where multiple instances of an application need to coordinate access to shared resources. For example, in an e-commerce dashboard, when processing inventory updates during a flash sale, a distributed lock ensures only one server processes the stock reduction for a specific product ID, preventing overselling. Similarly, in a banking application's transaction processing panel, distributed locks prevent duplicate transfers when multiple users attempt to transfer funds from the same account simultaneously. This pattern is also used in scheduled job runners across cloud infrastructure to ensure critical maintenance tasks like database backups don't run concurrently on different servers.
